title: fix: fresh guest PR preparation reports unsaved work
body: Fixes #185747. ## What Problem This Solves A guest continuing an owned pull request from an empty conversation can receive a dirty-work refusal before any PR source is applied. Native sandbox setup creates the protected `skills` and `.agents/skills` directories after the managed workspace baseline is captured. Initial PR admission then compares an empty canonical manifest with a projection containing those generated directories and rejects it as unsaved work. ## User Impact The first PR import can accept the fresh workspace once its generated layout is settled. Existing checks for staged, dirty, untracked and unpublished work, current requester identity, and PR eligibility remain in force. Protected skill mounts retain their existing permissions, and authored directories retain their existing preservation policy. ## Why This Change Was Made The layout producer now reports whether it created a protected source directory. Managed layout preparation completes the existing workspace checkpoint in that case, before the sandbox is exposed to its caller. Repeated preparation with existing directories adds no checkpoint. The shared layout path covers both execution and workspace-information callers. This keeps the correction with the producer and its existing settlement owner. The pristine comparison, Git checks, directory exclusions, schemas and configuration are unchanged. The tests join actual sandbox layout to the registered PR preparation action, which the earlier clean-empty fixture did not exercise. ## Evidence On the base, the joined regression returned the exact dirty-work error. A pass-through observation measured an empty canonical manifest and exactly three directory nodes in the projection (`.agents`, `.agents/skills`, `skills`); the production comparison returned false after the earlier Git guards passed. On the candidate, all 18 PR-preparation cases and 28 mount cases pass. The new cases verify first admission of the exact PR source, refusal and preservation of a newly authored empty directory, exclusion of a cache-only ancestor, and preservation of existing protected-source contents. Existing staged/dirty/untracked/unpublished, wrong-author and changed-identity controls remain green. GitHub and container transport are synthetic in these tests; the layout, workspace owner, manifests and registered import path execute normally. Changed-file formatting/lint and the selected production, test, UI, extension and tooling type checks passed remotely. The remaining 685 affected-caller tests across 38 files also passed, for 731 tests across 40 selected files. Their native E2E runtime build passed as a prerequisite. The PR-preparation file took 196.45 seconds including transformation and its existing Git/SQLite lifecycle cases; the mount file took 2.39 seconds. The broader owner boundary is necessary because isolated tests missed this composition. Hosted CI completed successfully on the exact head, including its selected runtime and UI jobs. On the running Gateway with a real required Docker sandbox, one fresh intent-only conversation followed by one UI-submitted preparation request now passes initial admission and saves the verified PR source. All 11 canonical Git blobs and projected files match the selected PR tree byte-for-byte, including executable bits. The remote fixture PR remains unchanged. **The complete native operation still returns `ok: false` at the later sandbox review-base stage.** Its result explicitly says that source integration is saved. This PR repairs the initial false pristine-workspace refusal; the later review-base failure remains unresolved and is being qualified separately. No retry or after-result model tool was used, and the partial fixture is preserved. The independent engineering review and canonical Auto Review are clean. Hosted CI is green on the exact head. These live personas are synthetic post-login fixtures; the evidence does not establish real OAuth admission or hostile-host isolation. ## Visual evidence []() | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![Before: generated layout causes the initial dirty\-work refusal](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/47e6cca3-d55a-479d-a6bc-0014ee74292d) | ![After: source integration is saved; a later review\-base failure remains](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ae028b6f-74c5-4261-8960-979dc1cb8e9b) | ### One first\-use preparation: source saved, then later review\-base failure https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3f70e240-255c-466f-a671-ffcee21cf619 ### Visual verification - Baseline: cbac30f3b63366a37ed583ad2f03c0e2eef2c0c7 - Exact head: `75e316cec08f4e4bbf264e0136b7579ba971f9ae` - Scenario: Start an ordinary linked guest conversation, wait for the PR link, then submit the owned PR through the composer and run prepare\_pr once\. Fresh equivalent conversations use the same persona and PR\. - Runtime/build: OpenClaw 2026\.10\.7, build 2026\.10\.7\-75e316cec08f\-2026\-10\-27T10\-20\-03\.468Z; running Gateway with required Docker sandbox; synthetic post\-login identity\. - Preparation submissions: 1 in each fresh conversation; no retry or after\-result model tools - Initial admission: Before: pristine refusal\. After: verified PR source accepted\. - Source preservation check: 11 of 11 canonical Git blobs and projection files match the verified PR tree byte\-for\-byte, including executable bits\. - Final operation outcome: ok:false at later sandbox review\-base preparation; complete preparation is not claimed\. - Exact reviewed head and running Gateway build/boot qualified before the fixed capture\. - First intent\-only turn settled without worktree or tool use; later request entered through the real composer\. - All 756 raw and sanitized fixed frames inspected; native result unchanged outside sidebar mask and factual Enter cue\. - Same 1440x1000 viewport, light theme, zoom and framing; separate fresh session identifiers are intentional\. - Remote fixture PR remains open at its original branch/head\. - Synthetic identity proof does not establish real OAuth admission or hostile\-host isolation\.
